lessons.title: Work, study and daily tasks
lessons.description: Talk about work, study and common tasks.

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: Where do you work?
B: I work in an office.
A: Do you have a meeting today?
B: Yes, at nine o’clock.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Use “I work” for a routine. Use “I am working” for an activity happening now.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: With I, use the base verb: I work.

quiz.question: What is a colleague?
quiz.explanation: A colleague is someone you work with.

lessons.title: Talking about last weekend
lessons.description: Describe completed activities using common past-simple verbs.

vocabulary.example: We visited our friends on Friday.

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: What did you do last weekend?
B: I visited my family and went to the market.
A: Did you enjoy it?
B: Yes, I did.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: In past questions, use did + the base verb: Did you go?

quiz.question: Choose the correct question.
quiz.explanation: After did, use the base form go.

quiz.question: Past form of buy:
quiz.explanation: Buy is irregular; its past form is bought.

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: What is the weather like?
B: It is cold and rainy.
A: Take your jacket.
B: Good idea, thank you.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Use “It is…” to describe weather: It is sunny. It is cold.

quiz.question: Which word describes wet weather?
quiz.explanation: Rainy means that rain is falling or likely.

quiz.question: Complete: It ___ cold today.
quiz.explanation: Use “it is” to describe the weather.

lessons.title: Making appointments
lessons.description: Arrange a meeting and respond politely.

vocabulary.example: I have an appointment at ten.

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: Are you available on Tuesday?
B: I am available after two.
A: Shall we meet at three?
B: That is convenient.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: “Could we…?” and “Would … be convenient?” are polite ways to arrange a meeting.

quiz.question: Choose a polite suggestion.
quiz.explanation: Could we…? is a polite suggestion.

quiz.question: What does reschedule mean?
quiz.explanation: To reschedule is to arrange a new date or time.

lessons.title: Health problems and advice
lessons.description: Describe common symptoms and understand everyday advice.

vocabulary.example: A cough can be a symptom.

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: What is wrong?
B: I have a headache.
A: You should rest.
B: Thank you.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Use should + base verb to give advice: You should rest.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Use should followed by the base verb.

quiz.question: A headache is a…
quiz.explanation: A headache is a symptom.

lessons.title: Giving opinions and reasons
lessons.description: Express an opinion, support it with reasons and disagree politely.

vocabulary.example: In my view, practice is essential.
The plan is useful; however, it is expensive.
The road was closed; therefore, we arrived late.
Although it was difficult, we finished.

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: In my view, online lessons save time.
B: I agree to some extent. However, classroom practice is also useful.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Use however to introduce contrast and therefore to introduce a result.

quiz.question: Which connector introduces a result?
quiz.explanation: Therefore introduces a consequence or result.

quiz.question: Choose a polite disagreement.
options: I see your point, but I have a different view.
quiz.explanation: This phrase acknowledges the other person before disagreeing.

lessons.title: Transport and travel
lessons.description: Ask about transport, tickets and travel times.

vocabulary.example: The bus stop is near the bank.
The train leaves from platform two.
Can I have a return ticket?

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: Excuse me, where is the bus station?
B: Go straight and turn left.
A: Thank you. How much is a ticket?
B: It is five pounds.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Use “Where is…?” to ask for a place and “How much is…?” to ask for a price.

quiz.question: Which phrase asks about price?
quiz.explanation: How much is…? asks about cost.

quiz.question: A platform is usually found at a…
quiz.explanation: Passengers wait on a platform at a station.

lessons.title: Asking for help politely
lessons.description: Use simple polite expressions when asking for help.

vocabulary.example: I do not understand this word.

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: Could you help me, please?
B: Of course. What do you need?
A: Could you repeat that slowly?
B: Certainly.

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: Could you…? is a polite way to make a request. Add please to sound friendly.

quiz.question: Choose a polite request.
quiz.explanation: Could you… please? is polite and natural.

quiz.question: What does repeat mean?
quiz.explanation: Repeat means to say or do something again.

lessons.title: Ordering food at a restaurant
lessons.description: Order food, ask about ingredients and request the bill.

vocabulary.example: Could I see the menu, please?
I would like to order soup.
Can I have salad as a side dish?
Could we have the bill, please?

sections.heading: Useful dialogue
sections.body:
A: Are you ready to order?
B: Yes, I would like chicken and rice.
A: Would you like a drink?
B: Water, please. And could we have the bill later?

sections.heading: Language tip
sections.body: “I would like…” is a polite way to order. Use “Could we have…?” to request something.

quiz.question: Which phrase politely asks for the bill?
options: Could we have the bill, please?
quiz.explanation: Could we have… please? is polite and clear.

quiz.question: Ingredients are…
options: The items used to make food
quiz.explanation: Ingredients are the foods or substances used in a dish.

lessons.title: Writing a clear professional email
lessons.description: Write concise professional emails with a clear request and next step.

vocabulary.example: I am writing regarding your request.
Thank you in advance for your help.

sections.heading: Email example
sections.body:
Dear Ms Lee,
I am writing regarding the meeting scheduled for Thursday. Could you please clarify the start time? I have attached the updated agenda.
Kind regards,
Alex

sections.heading: Writing tip
sections.body: Use a meaningful subject, put the request near the beginning, and explain the next step. Keep each paragraph focused on one idea.

quiz.question: Which phrase refers to a document sent with an email?
quiz.explanation: Attached describes a file included with the message.

quiz.question: What makes a professional email clearer?
options: A clear request and next step
quiz.explanation: A clear purpose and next step help the reader respond.
